NUM_PLANTED = 10
SENTS_PER_DOC = 12

PERTURB_EVERY = 8

    "restless", "fragile", "sturdy", "gentle", "curious", "fierce", "mellow", "crisp",

    "beacon", "valley", "cipher", "prairie", "atlas", "ember", "willow", "summit",
    "voyage", "archive", "horizon", "thicket", "current", "marble",
]

    "trembles", "widens", "echoes", "harden", "softens", "awakens", "dissolves",
    "climbs", "descends", "repeats", "returns", "frays", "bloom",
]
_ABSTRACT = [
    "memory", "silence", "distance", "patience", "fortune", "gravity", "reason",
    "season", "purpose", "balance",
]

# Sentence templates: {a}=adjective, {n}=noun, {v}=verb, {x}=abstract noun.
# Slots are frequent on purpose: no four consecutive literal tokens exist, so
# unrelated documents rarely agree on an entire 4-gram.

    "a {n} remembers the {a} {x} while the {v}",
    "near the {a} {n} a {a} {x} {v} again",
    "every {a} {n} keeps a {a} {x} that {v}",
    "the {n} and the {a} {x} {v} toward the {a} {n}",

    "each {n} carries a {a} {x} the way a {n} {v}",
    "when the {a} {x} {v} the whole {n} turns {a}",
    "the {n} {v} although the {a} {x} remains {a}",
    "above the {a} {n} an {a} {x} slowly {v}",
    "wherever a {a} {n} {v} the {x} follows the {n}",
    "the {a} {x} and the {a} {n} {v} without a {n}",
    "a single {n} {v} while every {a} {x} {v} onward",
    "before the {n} {v} the {a} {x} had already grown {a}",
    "along the {a} {n} the {x} of each {a} {n} {v}",
    "some {a} {x} {v} until the {n} itself becomes {a}",
    "the {a} {n} waits for a {x} that never {v}",
    "one {a} {n} after another {v} into the {a} {x}",

    out = list(tokens)

        if out[idx] in _ADJ:
            kind = _ADJ
        elif out[idx] in _NOUN or out[idx] in _ABSTRACT:

        elif out[idx] in _VERB:

        docs_tokens.append(_perturb(rng, docs_tokens[src]))
        planted.append((src, dup_idx))
    return [" ".join(toks) for toks in docs_tokens], planted

    (C(200,2) = 19,900 pairs) and extrapolate to 600 documents by scaling with
    the exact pair-count ratio:
        T_600_est = T_200 * C(600,2) / C(200,2) = T_200 * 9.0302...
    Justification: brute force is O(n^2) in pair count with essentially
    constant per-pair cost (set intersections over ~equal-size sets), so total
    time scales with the number of pairs. This is an estimate of true runtime,
    not a trick to inflate the speedup: we report it as such, and the equality
    test elsewhere runs brute force on ALL 600 docs for real.
"""

import time

from gen_essays import generate, NUM_DOCS, SEED
import dupdetect as dd

SUBSET_N = 200          # brute force is timed on this many documents ...
EXTRAPOLATE = ((NUM_DOCS * (NUM_DOCS - 1)) // 2) / ((SUBSET_N * (SUBSET_N - 1)) // 2)
